title: p256-ecdlp: parallel Pollard rho on negation classes with a sigma walk

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and input Q=[x]P on NIST P-256 the parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho algorithm in proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39. It walks on the negation classes {W, −W} of P-256, using 2^32 walks and 2^16 adders, with batched affine additions. Walks run in trails from fresh coins: each trail ends at its first distinguished point, which it records once, including a distinguished point first reached during a look-ahead, and the first key match is resolved by replaying both trails, so a degenerate match has probability exactly 1/r (Lemmas R and D). A fruitless cycle is escaped to twice the canonical point of its least-key member, a doubling with no table, so the point after an escape is fresh given the cycle; a trail is not trapped (Lemma T, and Lemma L for re-entry into an escaped cycle). Fruitless cycles are escaped only after exact checks, and the distinguished-point test comes first on every point. Total computation is at most 2^127.370918 target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, distinguished-point storage and lookup, all failures and restarts, collision replay, verification and output. Each walk step pays its common-path count, 847 instructions, and a Markov reserve of 40.90 for rare work, that is 887.90 instructions per walk step at C=1000. Rare work is charged at forced-path maxima, measured with a bounding build of each unbatched operation, and the meter aborts when the metered rare work exceeds 64 times its expectation, with probability at most 1/64 (counted in delta). Peak memory is at most 2^76.542441 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^47.949581 units and is included in total work. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack on one target with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. The success bound of 0.395898 is the model bound 0.411524 less 1/64 for the meter and 2^-20 for the other terms. It relies on the disclosed heuristics H1-H3 in proof.md: H1 is the standard random-mapping model for r-adding class walks; H2 is the fresh-class premise (a class reached for the first time is uniform and independent, including classes reached after an escape), from which Lemma C, Lemma T and the per-event rates follow; H3 is the representativeness of the measured instruction counts of the common path, with rare work charged at forced-path maxima. These are supported by toy-curve runs of the identical procedure and by production-curve measurements, not proved. This is a carefully accounted generic attack, not a claim of a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the complete procedure of proof.md section 1.3 on random prime-order toy curves y^2=x^3-3x+b (the P-256 shape), at budget tau = tau_e4/10^4: each slot runs trails from fresh coins without tracking coefficients, with the same class key, canonical rule, adder images and index, both cycle rules and escapes; a trail ends at its first distinguished point, recorded once with its coins, or is abandoned at the cap; each slot takes L steps and finishes its trail. The first key match is resolved by replaying both trails from their coins (with a different anchor schedule, checking Lemma R); a degenerate match fails. The filters compare keys masked to filter_bits, as the kernels keep only 64 key bits, and the distinguished-point test precedes every escape and every look-ahead step; with check_all_replays every recorded trail is also replayed and any replay that misses its recorded point is counted. Reports the success rate against 1-exp(-tau), degenerate matches and replay mismatches. No oracle collision table. Toy scale only: it tests the procedure and its collision statistics, not production cost.
